result.title: Could this potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments? #TEDTalks
result.description: What if medicines could "speak" directly to your cells? Protein designer and TED Fellow Chris Bahl introduces a new generation of miniproteins: AI-designed medicines that can deliver detailed instructions to fix what's making you sick. He shares how this breakthrough could potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments for some of humanity's most challenging diseases.

result.title: Why Great Art Requires Risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth and Robert Vargas | TED
result.description:
Van Halen drummer and co-founder Alex Van Halen and lead singer David Lee Roth sit down with visual artist Robert Vargas, who paints freehand murals up to twenty stories tall, to reveal the two-step recipe behind great art: do your homework, then break every rule. Along the way, they swap stories about heartbreak, good luck charms — and why you should rehearse for what goes wrong. (Recorded at TEDxFargo on July 29, 2026)

result.title: Want Someone to Change? Ask This Question | Philip Jameson | TED
result.description:
Why is it so hard to get someone to change? Leadership expert Philip Jameson has spent years watching people pitch smart ideas at work, only to be met with colleagues resistant to adjusting how things get done. He breaks down why people push back against change — and the one question that could help your next idea take flight. (Recorded at TED@BCG on August 18, 2026)

result.title: Why Clean Energy Is an Unstoppable Force | Michael Liebreich | TED
result.description:
Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing? Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again. Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required. The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected. (Recorded at TED Countdown: The Next Ten on October 15, 2026)

result.title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks
result.description: Do you avoid talking to people you disagree with? Author and mediator Emily Kasriel thinks you should try it out. She explains why engaging with ideas that bother you is one of the most powerful things you can do — and presents her framework for “deep listening” that can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and political divides.
